lines.text: Picture a driver nearing a stop line. How fast should they go?
They weigh three things: the speed limit, "can I still stop?", and creeping in at the end.
Our robot asks the same three, every loop.
Speed one: top speed, four meters per second.
Speed two: the fastest speed it can still stop from, in the distance left.
Speed three: gentle, a number times the distance. It only matters in the last third of a meter.
Then take the smallest of the three.
Far away, top speed is smallest, so it cruises.
Then "can I still stop" takes over, and it brakes along a smooth curve.
At the very end, the gentle line takes over, and it glides in.
One more trick. A driver needs a moment to react before braking.
So does our robot: its readings are slightly old, and commands take time to reach the motors.
So it brakes a twentieth of a second early.
And within three millimeters, about two stacked pennies, it asks for zero.
